citation.authors: Semnani-Azad Z, Khan TA, Chiavaroli L, Chen V et al

cited_by.title: Intermittent fasting for weight and health

record.population: Adults in 99 randomised trials (720 healthy, 5,862 with health conditions)
record.design: Systematic review and network meta-analysis of intermittent fasting (alternate-day, time-restricted, whole-day) against continuous calorie restriction or eating freely
record.finding: All fasting and calorie-restriction diets reduced weight compared with eating freely. Compared with continuous calorie restriction, only alternate-day fasting gave extra weight loss (1.29 kg, moderate certainty). In trials of 24 weeks or longer, strategies only beat eating freely.
record.note: Mostly short trials. Ethnicity not reported in the abstract.
